conceptual.anchor: MDL as a model-selection criterion motivated by optimal coding: choose the parsimonious model. ... we must not equate shorter = true. MDL is a selection criterion, not a truth oracle.

formal.anchor: support / confidence / lift ... architecture change + database migration -> integration test modification. If the relationship repeatedly occurs, KnowledgeOS could surface it as: Observed association NOT: causal rule.

governance.anchor: Zero tells us when learning should not start. ... Leonardo tells us whether the learning problem has been sufficiently contextualized. ... Statistical Learning tells us how to learn once those conditions are satisfied.

lexical.anchor: Do not import 'machine learning' into KnowledgeOS as a bounded context. Extract the underlying reasoning patterns and turn only the domain-relevant ones into KnowledgeOS methods. ... Assessment is not the same thing as Observation, Evidence, Recommendation, or Decision.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Both source book-extractions are complementary catalogues of transferable statistical-learning patterns for KnowledgeOS with almost no specific-technique overlap -- likely intended as companion documents rather than one superseding the other.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: The group_evidence note explicitly identifies A as 'a second, differently-organized extraction from The Elements of Statistical Learning' -- the identical source book B is drawn from (B's own alias is 'Elements of Statistical Learning extraction'). A organizes its material around a new InferenceProblem domain concept, a MethodSelector domain service, and an EP-00..EP-16 technique catalogue with Zero-Lens gates G0-G9, none of which appear in B's rows (which instead catalogue association-rule mining, Apriori pruning, graphical-model edge semantics, FDR control, Bayes decision theory, bias-variance tradeoff). No row in either sample cites the other by name, but the note's explicit 'second extraction from the same book' framing shows A was produced as a follow-on pass over the same source territory B already covers.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If A's extraction (S0472) predates B's (S0469/S0833) rather than following it, the 'second pass' framing would need reversing, though the EXTENSION relationship (different, additive organizing framework over the same source) would likely still hold either direction.

rationale_evidence.anchor: assessment must be separated from construction; assessment must respect its evidence boundary; leakage invalidates assessment; complexity affects stability; uncertainty should be measurable; discovery is not authority; association is not causation; structure depends on the chosen similarity model; relationships have semantics; aggregation requires independence awareness; and large-scale discovery requires explicit false-discovery control.
rationale_evidence.statement: Bottom-line synthesis statement listing the eleven transferable facts as the actual value of the book for KnowledgeOS, explicitly contrasted with importing specific algorithms (Random Forest, Lasso, PCA, SVM).

Bias-variance tradeoff (more complex models generally reduce bias but increase variance) is adopted as an architectural principle for model/reasoning-method routing: ModelSelection=f(Bias,Variance,Loss,Context,Cost), giving BiggerModel ⇏ BetterKnowledge. Notes that squared bias can be substantial while classification error remains zero if the estimate stays on the correct side of a decision boundary, so ModelError ≠ DecisionError and SmallModelError ⇏ CorrectDecision — motivating a distinction between Prediction Quality, Decision Quality, and Knowledge Quality as three non-collapsible things (Prediction -> Decision -> Knowledge claim).

Final assessment: the book should not be adopted as an 'ML methods' reference but as a candidate Inference Theory layer — a formal bridge from epistemically-admissible-context to decision-loss to model-selection to generalization to uncertainty to assurance; the underlying discipline (assumptions->representation->model->loss->fitting->generalization->validation->uncertainty->selection) maps to KnowledgeOS even though specific techniques (Lasso, SVM, Random Forest, boosting, neural networks, PCA, k-means) are not themselves adopted.
